title: ShareRecon scripts - operator notes
text:
ShareRecon scripts - operator notes
Owner: Hector Salas, Systems Engineer (IT)
Last updated: Tue 2026-07-14

Purpose
ShareRecon is the set of nightly scripts that reconcile share and loan balances from CoreBanking against the general ledger. It is a legacy system. The scripts are shell plus Python, and they run on the IT batch host. Their output is the morning exception report that Operations works from. These notes are for whoever is on call when it breaks.

Schedule
The CoreBanking vendor drops the end-of-day extract files to our SFTP landing folder. The usual arrival time is between 1:15 and 1:45 AM ET. A cron job on the batch host kicks off ShareRecon at 2:30 AM ET. A normal run takes 20-35 minutes.

The exception report is emailed to Operations (Rita Solano, Larry Bernard) by about 3:15 AM. A copy is written to the recon share folder. On month-end nights the run can take close to an hour because of the interest accrual postings.

Inputs
1. CoreBanking share trial balance extract (daily, fixed-width)
2. CoreBanking loan trial balance extract (daily, fixed-width)
3. GL posting file from CoreBanking for the business date
4. Suspense and clearing account mapping table (maintained by Operations, stored in the recon config folder)

All three extracts must carry the same business date in the header record. The script checks this and should abort if the dates don't match. In practice it only logs a warning.

Known failure modes
Late extract. This is the most common failure. If the vendor files land after 2:30, the cron job runs against the previous night's files, or against partial files. The result is a batch of false GL differences, usually 4-10 lines in the share suspense and dividend payable accounts.

Mapping table drift. When Operations adds a new GL account and the mapping table isn't updated, the new account shows up as an unmatched difference every night until someone fixes the table.

ACH and card settlement timing. Items that post to clearing accounts after the CoreBanking cutoff show up as differences. They self-clear the next day, so check the clearing account aging before escalating.

Disk space. The batch host log volume fills up roughly every quarter. Check the free space if the job exits with no report.

Re-run steps
1. Confirm all three extract files are in the landing folder with the correct business date in the header.
2. Move the bad output to the recon archive folder and add an _invalid suffix.
3. Run the manual wrapper script from the ShareRecon directory with the business date argument.
4. Compare the new exception count to the original run. Note both counts in the IT ticket.
5. Email the corrected report to Operations and reply in the #it thread if one exists.

If the differences remain after a clean re-run, treat them as real. Hand them to Operations for investigation.

Open items
We want the script to hard-fail on a date mismatch instead of warning, and to poll for file arrival instead of relying on a fixed cron time. Neither is scheduled yet.

title: Online Banking Support Guide
text:
Online Banking Support Guide
Author: Maxwell Castro, Teller, Member Services
Last updated: 2026-07-14

Purpose
This guide gives front-line staff a consistent way to handle member questions about online and mobile banking. It covers what to check first, what we can fix at the teller line, and when to hand off. It is written from the teller perspective, so Member Advocates and Member Services Representatives may have additional tools. If something here conflicts with direction from Paul Jensen, follow Paul and let me know so I can update the guide.

How the Systems Fit Together
OnlineBanking is the member-facing online and mobile banking platform. It is a critical system owned by Information Technology. It depends on CoreBanking, which is our vendor-hosted core for share and loan processing, and on MemberSSO, which handles member identity and MFA. This matters because most problems show up in one of three ways:

1. A member cannot sign in or gets stuck on the MFA step. This usually points to MemberSSO or a member-side issue such as a new phone or an old browser.
2. A member can sign in but balances or recent transactions look wrong or stale. This usually points to CoreBanking or a posting delay, not to OnlineBanking itself.
3. The whole site or app is unavailable for many members at once. This is an outage and goes to IT right away.

First Checks Before Escalating
Work through these in order and note each one in the member's record.

Confirm who you are talking to. Verify identity using the standard verification steps in the teller procedures before discussing any online banking details. Never ask a member to read out a password or full MFA code to you, and never type one on their behalf.

Ask what the member sees. Get the exact error text and whether it happens on the app, the website, or both. Ask when it started and whether anything changed, such as a new device, a password reset, or an updated phone number.

Check whether it is just this member. If two or more members report the same symptom within a short window, treat it as a possible system issue. Check #it for any posted notice before you do anything else.

Try the basics. Have the member update the mobile app, clear the browser cache or try a different browser, and confirm the device clock and time zone are correct, since MFA codes can fail when the clock is off.

What Tellers Can Do
We can explain how to use features such as transfers, statements, and bill pay, and we can walk members through enrolling or re-enrolling. We can confirm that a transaction has posted in CoreBanking and explain the difference between pending and posted items. We can start a password reset request through the approved process.

What Tellers Cannot Do
We cannot change MFA methods, unlock a flagged login, or override a security hold. Those go to a Member Advocate. We also cannot promise a fix time on a system problem. Say that we have passed it to the right team and will follow up.

Handoff Paths
Security or locked access: hand to a Member Advocate such as Zachary Powers, Joanna Buchanan, or Nichole Kirk. Include what you verified and the exact symptom.

Suspected fraud or an unfamiliar login the member did not make: stop troubleshooting, reassure the member, and hand to a Member Advocate immediately. They will coordinate with Compliance if needed.

System or outage issues: post in #it with the time, the symptom, the platform, and how many members you have seen. Andre Dubois manages IT and the team will take it from there. Also tell Paul Jensen so the floor is aware.

A member who is only asking about a specific loan or share balance: confirm in CoreBanking directly, since it is the system of record.

Writing Good Notes
If we need to refer to a member in a note or a message, use the member's internal client id or the approved name field in the record rather than copying personal details into chat. Do not paste account numbers, phone numbers, or full emails into #member-services or #it. Describe the issue and let the receiving team look up the record.

When the Outage Is Real
If OnlineBanking is confirmed down, use the approved script: we are aware of an issue with online and mobile banking, our technology team is working on it, and branch and phone services are available. Offer in-branch help for urgent needs like transfers or balance checks. Do not speculate on cause. Remember that if CoreBanking is affected, other services that depend on it may also be slow, so keep an eye on #it for updates.

Follow-Up
If you told a member you would follow up, log it and close the loop the same day when possible. Send suggestions for improving this guide to Maxwell Castro.

title: Card Dispute Procedures
text:
Card Dispute Procedures
Owner: Timothy Harris, Payments Specialist, Operations
Last updated: 2026-08-05
Audience: Member Services, Operations, Compliance

Purpose
This procedure describes how Brightwater Credit Union intakes, investigates, and resolves debit card disputes raised by members. It covers unauthorized transactions, duplicate charges, incorrect amounts, merchandise or service not received, and ATM errors. It also explains where ACH-related disputes differ, since members often confuse the two.

Systems Involved
CardProcessor is the debit card authorization feed owned by Operations. It is the source of record for authorization history, merchant descriptors, and decline codes. CardProcessor depends on CoreBanking, so if CoreBanking is degraded, authorization data and provisional credit postings may lag. Check #it before assuming a transaction is missing.
ACHHub handles ACH origination and receipt, also owned by Operations. Disputes about ACH debits (for example, a recurring withdrawal the member says was not authorized) are NOT handled under the card dispute process. See the section on ACH disputes below.
MemberCRM is where Member Services logs relationship notes on every dispute contact. Record the call, the member's stated reason, and any commitments you made.

Step 1: Intake (Member Services)
The Teller, Member Services Representative, or Member Advocate who first speaks with the member does the following:
1. Verify the member through the standard identity check. Never ask the member to read out a full card number. Reference the card by the last four digits shown in CoreBanking only.
2. Identify the transaction in CardProcessor by date, amount, and merchant descriptor.
3. Ask whether the card is still in the member's possession. If there is any chance of compromise, request an immediate card block and reissue before anything else.
4. Complete the dispute intake form and attach any member-supplied documents, such as receipts or merchant correspondence.
5. Log the contact in MemberCRM with the dispute reference and the date.
If the dispute is escalated, a Member Advocate (Zachary Powers, Joanna Buchanan, or Nichole Kirk) takes ownership. Paul Jensen is the backstop for unresolved member complaints.

Step 2: Operations Review
Within one business day of intake, Operations picks up the case. The Payments Specialist reviews the authorization record in CardProcessor and confirms:
- Whether the transaction was chip, PIN, contactless, or card-not-present
- Whether the merchant has a history of reversals on the same amount
- Whether the amount matches the authorization or was adjusted at settlement
Larry Bernard, Settlements Specialist, checks settlement files to confirm whether the item has fully cleared. Rita Solano, Operations Manager, approves any case above $2,500 or any case flagged as potential fraud ring activity.

Step 3: Provisional Credit
Regulation E timelines apply to unauthorized electronic transfers. Operations must either finish the investigation or issue provisional credit within 10 business days of the member's notice. For new accounts or point-of-sale transactions, extended timelines may apply, but check with Compliance before relying on them. Provisional credit is posted in CoreBanking by Operations, and the member is notified by Member Services the same day. Document the credit amount and date in the case record.

Step 4: Merchant Chargeback
If the dispute is valid, Operations files a chargeback through the card network using the evidence gathered. Keep a copy of the filing and the network's acknowledgment. Merchant responses are typically due within 30 days. If the merchant represents the item with evidence, the Payments Specialist reviews it and decides whether to accept or file for arbitration. Arbitration requires Rita Solano's sign-off because of network fees.

Step 5: Resolution and Member Notice
Once a decision is made, Member Services contacts the member by phone and sends written notice. If the dispute is decided in the member's favor, provisional credit becomes permanent. If not, Operations reverses the provisional credit after giving the member written notice and the required advance period, and Member Services explains the reasoning plainly. Close the MemberCRM note with the outcome.

ACH Disputes
Unauthorized ACH debits follow a different clock and different return reason codes. Route these to Operations as an ACHHub return request, not a card dispute. The Payments Specialist submits the return within the allowed window, which is short for consumer unauthorized returns, so escalate the same day. If the member says the originator is still pulling funds, advise the member to also contact the originator and consider a stop payment.

Compliance Escalation
Notify Wesley Tran or Monica Feld in Compliance if any of the following apply:
- Three or more disputes from the same member in 90 days
- Disputes that cluster around one merchant across multiple members
- Any sign of account takeover or synthetic identity activity
BSAWatch monitors related patterns, but a human referral from the floor is often the earliest warning, so do not wait for an alert.

Record Keeping
Retain the full case file, including evidence, provisional credit records, and member notices, for the period required by Compliance. Do not paste card numbers, account numbers, or member identity details into Slack or email. Use the dispute reference only.

Questions
Contact Timothy Harris in Operations or post in #member-services for floor-level questions.

title: Incident Response Plan
text:
Incident Response Plan
Owner: Andre Dubois, IT Manager
Last updated: 2026-08-07
Applies to: All Brightwater Credit Union staff and the systems owned by Information Technology, Operations, Lending, Compliance, and Member Services

Purpose
This plan describes how Brightwater Credit Union detects, classifies, escalates, and closes out technology and operational incidents. It exists so that everyone knows who is in charge, who gets called, and what gets written down when something breaks. It does not replace vendor runbooks for CoreBanking, which is vendor hosted, but it tells us how we engage the vendor and how we protect members while we wait.

What counts as an incident
An incident is any unplanned event that degrades or interrupts a system, exposes member or credit union data, or prevents a required control from running. Examples: members cannot log in to OnlineBanking, the debit card authorization feed stops responding, ACH files fail to transmit, or the nightly reconciliation does not finish.

Severity levels
Sev 1: A critical system is down or a confirmed data exposure is under way. Critical systems are CoreBanking, OnlineBanking, MemberSSO, CardProcessor, ACHHub, and BSAWatch.
Sev 2: A critical system is degraded, or a standard system (LoanDesk, CreditPull, MemberCRM) is down for more than one hour during business hours.
Sev 3: A legacy or standard system has a limited issue with a workaround, or a single-team impact.
Sev 4: Cosmetic or low-impact issue that can be handled in the normal queue.

Dependency check
Before declaring scope, the responder checks the dependency chain. An outage in CoreBanking will also hit OnlineBanking, CardProcessor, ACHHub, LoanDesk, BSAWatch, and ShareRecon. An outage in MemberSSO will affect OnlineBanking and MemberCRM. A failure in ACHHub also affects BSAWatch. Declare the root system first so that we do not open duplicate incidents for downstream symptoms.

Roles
Incident Commander: Andre Dubois by default. If he is unavailable, Hector Salas takes over. The commander owns decisions, timing of updates, and the incident log.
Technical Lead: Hector Salas for infrastructure and CoreBanking vendor contact, Shannon Sheppard for OnlineBanking and application issues, Amy Cole for data and reporting issues.
Operations Lead: Rita Solano for CardProcessor and ACHHub. Larry Bernard and Timothy Harris support settlement and payment decisions.
Compliance Lead: Wesley Tran, with Monica Feld and Chris Burgess for BSA/AML impact.
Member Communications: Paul Jensen coordinates the member services floor script and the branch and call center response.
Executive Sponsor: Gloria Ibarra is notified for every Sev 1 and any incident with potential regulatory or reputational impact.
People matters, such as staffing during a long incident, go through Michelle Perry.

Response steps
1. Detect and report. Anyone who sees a problem posts in #it and pages the on-call engineer. Do not wait to confirm.
2. Triage. The commander assigns a severity within 15 minutes and opens an incident thread in #it.
3. Contain. Stop the bleeding first: pause ACH file transmission, disable a suspect integration, or force a MemberSSO session reset as needed.
4. Communicate. Sev 1 updates go out every 30 minutes, Sev 2 every hour. Post internal updates in #general only after the commander approves the wording. Member Services receives a short script from Paul Jensen.
5. Recover. Restore service, validate with a test transaction, and confirm downstream systems have caught up.
6. Close. The commander confirms with each system owner before closing.

BSA/AML monitoring continuity
BSAWatch is a critical compliance control. If it is down or delayed, Wesley Tran must be told immediately. Compliance will document the gap, and once the system is restored, Monica Feld reviews the backlog of alerts in the private #bsa-aml channel. Chris Burgess prioritizes any alert that was queued during the outage. Any gap longer than one business day is assessed for regulatory reporting.

ShareRecon handling
ShareRecon is a legacy set of scripts that run nightly against CoreBanking. If a run fails, Hector Salas reruns it after CoreBanking is confirmed healthy and Amy Cole checks that share and GL totals agree. Rita Solano is told if unreconciled items remain at the start of the next business day, since settlement work depends on clean balances. Because the scripts are legacy, never edit them during an incident without the commander's approval and a saved copy.

Data exposure incidents
If member information may have been exposed, stop and tell Wesley Tran and Andre Dubois at once. Do not copy member data into Slack or email while investigating. Refer to records by internal ids only. Compliance decides on member and regulator notification.

Post-incident review
Within five business days of closing a Sev 1 or Sev 2, the commander holds a blameless review. The review covers timeline, root cause, what worked, and action items with owners and due dates. The write-up is stored with the incident log and reviewed by Wesley Tran when compliance is involved.

Plan maintenance
This plan is reviewed twice a year and after any Sev 1. Send suggested changes to Andre Dubois.

title: Vendor Management Policy
text:
Vendor Management Policy
Owner: Michelle Perry, HR Business Partner
Last updated: 2026-08-20
Applies to: All Brightwater Credit Union staff and teams

Purpose
Brightwater Credit Union relies on outside vendors to host core processing, move payments, pull credit, and support our staff. This policy sets out how we choose, onboard, monitor, and exit vendors so that member data stays protected, services stay available, and we meet regulatory expectations. It also defines who is responsible at each step.

Scope
This policy covers any third party that provides a service, software, hosting, data, or staffing to the credit union, including vendors behind CoreBanking (vendor hosted), CardProcessor, ACHHub, CreditPull, and the tools used by MemberSSO and OnlineBanking. It also covers consultants, temporary staffing agencies, and training providers engaged through HR.

Roles and Responsibilities
Gloria Ibarra, President and CEO, approves any new vendor relationship with a critical system or an annual commitment above $50,000, and signs the related contracts.
Wesley Tran, Chief Compliance Officer, owns the vendor risk program, maintains the vendor inventory, and reviews all due diligence results.
The business owner is the manager of the team that owns the affected system: Andre Dubois for IT systems, Rita Solano for Operations systems, Kara Nwosu for Lending systems, Paul Jensen for Member Services systems, and Wesley Tran for Compliance systems.
Michelle Perry manages vendors that supply HR services, temporary staff, and employee training, and confirms background screening and conduct requirements for vendor personnel who work on site.
Andre Dubois and Hector Salas review technical security, integration, and access requirements for any vendor that touches our network or data.

Vendor Tiering
Every vendor is assigned a tier based on the most sensitive system or data it supports.
Tier 1 (critical): supports a critical system such as CoreBanking, OnlineBanking, MemberSSO, CardProcessor, ACHHub, or BSAWatch, or holds member data.
Tier 2 (standard): supports a standard system such as LoanDesk, CreditPull, or MemberCRM.
Tier 3 (low): supports a legacy or non-member-facing function, or supplies goods and services with no data access.
The tier drives the depth of due diligence, how often we review the vendor, and the contract terms we require.

Due Diligence Before Selection
The business owner submits a vendor request to Compliance describing the need, the systems affected, and the data involved. Compliance then collects, at a minimum:
Financial statements for the last two years, or equivalent evidence of stability.
A current SOC 2 Type II report or comparable independent assurance for Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors.
Insurance certificates, including cyber liability coverage.
Business continuity and disaster recovery plans, with recovery time objectives that match the dependent system.
Subcontractor disclosures and the locations where data is stored or processed.
IT completes a security questionnaire and reviews how the vendor integrates with our systems. For example, any new service that depends on CoreBanking must be reviewed for the downstream effect on ShareRecon, ACHHub, and BSAWatch.

Contract Requirements
All Tier 1 and Tier 2 contracts must include: confidentiality and data protection obligations aligned with the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act; breach notification to Brightwater within 24 hours of discovery; service level targets with credits for missed targets; the right to audit or receive audit reports; regulator access to vendor records; subcontractor approval rights; and data return and deletion terms at exit. Legal review is arranged by Compliance before signature.

Onboarding and Access
Vendor accounts are requested by the business owner and created by IT with least-privilege access. Vendor staff sign in through MemberSSO-backed controls with multifactor authentication where supported. Shared accounts are not permitted. Access is reviewed quarterly, and removed within one business day when a vendor employee leaves the engagement.

Ongoing Monitoring
Tier 1 vendors are reviewed annually in full and checked quarterly for service levels, incidents, and open findings. Tier 2 vendors are reviewed every two years with an annual check on service levels. Tier 3 vendors are reviewed at renewal. Business owners record performance issues in the vendor inventory, and Compliance reports results to the CEO each quarter. Material changes, such as an acquisition of the vendor, a new data location, or a significant outage, trigger an immediate review.

Incident Handling
If a vendor reports or we detect an incident, the business owner notifies Compliance and IT right away. IT posts operational updates in #it, and Compliance decides whether regulator or member notification is required. Vendor incident details are kept out of public channels until Compliance confirms what can be shared.

Termination and Exit
Each Tier 1 contract must have a documented exit plan covering data return, transition support, and replacement options. On termination, IT disables all access and integrations, Compliance confirms certified data deletion, and the business owner updates the inventory.

Exceptions and Questions
Exceptions require written approval from the Chief Compliance Officer and the CEO. Questions about this policy can be sent to Michelle Perry or Wesley Tran.

title: BSA/AML Program Policy
text:
BSA/AML Program Policy
Owner: Compliance (Wesley Tran, Chief Compliance Officer)
Author: Chris Burgess, AML Investigator
Last updated: 2026-08-21

Purpose
This policy describes how Brightwater Credit Union meets its obligations under the Bank Secrecy Act and related anti-money laundering requirements. It sets out roles, monitoring practices, escalation paths, and recordkeeping expectations for every team that touches member transactions. It applies to all employees, including tellers, member advocates, lending staff, operations, and IT.

Program Structure
The program rests on five pillars: a system of internal controls, independent testing, a designated BSA Officer, ongoing training, and risk-based customer due diligence. Wesley Tran serves as the designated BSA Officer and reports program status to the CEO, Gloria Ibarra, and to the Board on a quarterly basis. Monica Feld (BSA/AML Analyst) and Chris Burgess (AML Investigator) carry out day-to-day monitoring and case work.

Roles and Responsibilities
Compliance owns BSAWatch, our BSA/AML monitoring platform, and is responsible for scenario tuning, alert triage, case management, and regulatory filings. Member Services is the first line of defense and is expected to note and report unusual activity observed at the branch, by phone, or through MemberCRM. Lending reports suspicious application patterns, such as inconsistent income documentation or unexplained third-party involvement, discovered in LoanDesk. Operations owns ACHHub and CardProcessor and must flag abnormal origination or settlement patterns. Information Technology maintains system availability and data feeds and supports investigations with data pulls on request.

Monitoring and Alert Handling
BSAWatch ingests transaction data from CoreBanking and ACH activity from ACHHub. Because of these dependencies, any outage or delay in either source can create monitoring gaps. Alerts are generated nightly and prioritized as high, medium, or low. Monica Feld performs first-level triage within one business day for all alerts. High-priority alerts must be reviewed the same business day. Alerts that cannot be closed as false positives are escalated to Chris Burgess for investigation. Each alert disposition must include a written rationale that references the specific scenario, the review performed, and the conclusion.

Monitoring Gaps
If CoreBanking or ACHHub experiences an outage, a delayed feed, or a failed batch, IT must notify Compliance in #it and directly to the BSA/AML team the same day. Compliance will document the gap, determine whether backfilled data is complete, and run a catch-up review before alerts are closed. Gaps lasting more than one business day must be reported to the BSA Officer for a determination on whether additional manual review is needed.

Customer Due Diligence
Member Services collects and verifies identifying information at account opening in line with the Customer Identification Program. Higher-risk relationships, including certain business accounts and members with unusual cash activity, receive enhanced due diligence. Enhanced reviews are documented in the case file and refreshed on a risk-based schedule. Staff must not tip off any member that a review or filing is under way.

Currency Transaction Reports
Tellers and Member Services staff must record cash transactions accurately so that aggregation across a business day is correct. Any cash activity over the reporting threshold requires a Currency Transaction Report, filed by Compliance within the regulatory deadline. Staff must not structure, or advise a member on structuring, transactions to avoid reporting. Suspected structuring must be reported internally right away.

Suspicious Activity Reporting
Any employee who observes potentially suspicious activity must submit an internal referral to Compliance on the same day. Referrals may be sent by email to the BSA/AML team or raised verbally to Monica Feld or Chris Burgess. Chris Burgess prepares the case narrative, and the BSA Officer approves the decision to file. Suspicious Activity Reports are filed within 30 calendar days of initial detection, extended to 60 days only when no suspect has been identified. Continuing activity reviews occur every 90 days while a pattern persists.

Confidentiality
The existence of a SAR, and any information that would reveal it, is strictly confidential. Discussion of cases is limited to the private #bsa-aml channel and to employees with a need to know. Never discuss case details in public channels such as #general, #member-services, or #lending. Do not record SAR references in MemberCRM notes.

Training
All employees complete annual BSA/AML training. New hires complete it within 30 days of their start date, coordinated by Michelle Perry in HR. Compliance staff and tellers receive additional role-specific training on typologies, structuring, and ACH-related fraud patterns.

Recordkeeping
BSA records, including CTRs, SARs, supporting documents, and case notes, are retained for at least five years from the date of filing or creation. Compliance maintains the retention schedule, and IT ensures that required data remains retrievable from CoreBanking and BSAWatch archives.

Independent Testing
An independent review of the program is conducted annually. Findings are tracked to closure by the BSA Officer, and policy updates resulting from testing are recorded in this document.

Questions
Direct questions about this policy to Chris Burgess or Wesley Tran in Compliance.

title: Member Identification Program (Customer Identification Program Policy)
text:
Brightwater Credit Union
Member Identification Program
Owner: Wesley Tran, Chief Compliance Officer
Last updated: 2026-09-04
Applies to: Member Services, Lending, Operations, Compliance, Information Technology

Purpose
This policy describes how Brightwater Credit Union verifies the identity of every person or entity that opens a share account, applies for a loan, or is added as a joint owner. It supports our obligations under the Bank Secrecy Act and the USA PATRIOT Act customer identification requirements, and it protects the credit union and our members from fraud and identity theft. Staff must follow this policy at every point of entry, whether in the branch, by phone, or through digital channels.

Scope
The program covers new members, new joint owners, new borrowers and co-borrowers, and members whose identity information must be re-verified because of a trigger event described below. It applies to both consumer and business relationships.

Required Information
Before an account is opened or a loan is funded, staff must collect the following for each individual: full legal name, date of birth, residential or business street address, and a taxpayer identification number. For non-individuals, staff collect the legal name, principal place of business, and the entity tax identification number, plus information on the people who control the entity and own a significant share of it. An account cannot be opened if any element is missing. Staff should never record these values in free-text notes in MemberCRM; they belong only in the structured fields in CoreBanking.

Verification Methods
Identity is verified using documents or non-documentary methods.

Documentary: an unexpired government-issued photo ID. Tellers and Member Services Representatives must inspect the original document, check for signs of alteration, and compare the photo to the person in front of them.

Non-documentary: for remote applications, verification runs through MemberSSO enrollment checks and the identity verification step in OnlineBanking account opening. For lending applicants, the bureau inquiry made through CreditPull in LoanDesk may serve as a supporting source, but it does not replace the required verification steps.

Where a document and a non-documentary result conflict, staff must use additional verification or escalate. Do not override a failed check on your own judgment.

Discrepancies and Escalation
If the information provided does not match a verification source, or if the documents appear altered, the employee must pause the account opening and notify a Member Advocate or the Member Services Manager, Paul Jensen. If fraud or identity theft is suspected, the matter goes to Compliance the same business day. The BSA/AML Analyst, Monica Feld, reviews the case and decides whether to refer it to the AML Investigator, Chris Burgess, for a possible suspicious activity report. Staff must not tell the individual that a referral has been made.

When Verification Cannot Be Completed
If identity cannot be reasonably verified within 30 days, the application is declined or the account is restricted to deposits only, as directed by Compliance. Funds are not disbursed on loans until verification is complete. The Lending Manager, Kara Nwosu, is responsible for confirming that no LoanDesk file is funded without a verification record.

Recordkeeping
For each verification, staff record the method used, the type of document and its issuing authority and expiration date, the result, and the name of the employee who performed the check. Copies of identifying documents are not retained in MemberCRM or on shared drives. Identification records are retained for five years after the account is closed, and verification results for rejected applications are retained for five years after the record is made. Information Technology owns retention controls in CoreBanking and will confirm each year that purge jobs follow this schedule.

Watchlist Screening
All new members and joint owners are screened against the OFAC sanctions list at account opening. BSAWatch also rescreens the member base on a recurring basis. Any potential match must be escalated to Compliance before any funds move through ACHHub or CardProcessor on the relationship. An OFAC match never gets resolved at the branch level.

Trigger Events for Re-Verification
Staff must re-verify identity when a member reports a change of name or taxpayer identification number, when MemberSSO flags a high-risk enrollment or credential reset, when mail is returned undeliverable more than once, or when BSAWatch generates an alert suggesting that the identity on file may not match the person using the account.

Training
All Member Services, Lending, and Operations staff complete identification training at hire and annually afterward. Michelle Perry in HR tracks completion, and Compliance reports completion rates to the CEO, Gloria Ibarra, each quarter.

Monitoring and Testing
Compliance samples new accounts and funded loans each month to confirm that verification records are complete and accurate. Exceptions are reported to the relevant team manager, who must document corrective action within 15 business days. Findings are summarized for the Board in the annual BSA/AML program review.

System Support
If a verification step in OnlineBanking or LoanDesk is unavailable, staff must not skip it. Use the manual documentary procedure and ask the IT Manager, Andre Dubois, for an expected restoration time through the #it channel. If CoreBanking is unavailable, accounts may not be opened.

Policy Review
The Chief Compliance Officer reviews this policy at least annually and whenever regulation or our systems change. Questions should go to Wesley Tran or the Compliance team.

title: Auto Lending Guidelines
text:
Auto Lending Guidelines
Owner: Kara Nwosu, Lending Manager
Last updated: 2026-09-18
Applies to: Lending team, Member Services, Compliance reviewers

Purpose
This guide describes how Brightwater Credit Union originates, underwrites, and funds consumer auto loans. It is meant for relationship managers, underwriters, analysts, and Member Services staff who refer members to Lending. If anything here conflicts with the Lending Policy approved by the board, the policy wins. Please flag the gap to me so I can correct this guide.

Systems Used
All auto applications are entered and tracked in LoanDesk. LoanDesk depends on CoreBanking for share and loan data and on CreditPull for bureau reports. If either is down, do not work around it by pulling reports outside the integration or booking loans manually. Post in #lending, notify Andre Dubois in IT via #it, and hold the application in its current status. Member relationship notes go in MemberCRM, which relies on MemberSSO, so notes may lag during an identity outage. Record the note in LoanDesk comments and copy it over later.

Application Intake
Applications may come from a branch, from online banking referral, or from a dealer. Member Services staff should confirm membership is active and share account is in good standing, then route the member to a relationship manager (Kathleen Smith or Martin Ford). Intake must capture the vehicle type (new, used, or refinance), requested term, requested amount, and stated income source. Do not collect documents by unsecured email. Use the secure upload link generated in LoanDesk.

Credit Pull Rules
One hard pull per application, authorized by the member in LoanDesk before the CreditPull request is sent. Rate shopping inside a 14-day window counts as a single inquiry for scoring purposes, but each pull still needs its own authorization on file. Never run a pull for curiosity or pre-screening without the member's consent.

Underwriting Standards
Rita Jimenez, Senior Underwriter, owns final decisions on anything outside the standard grid. Richard Marks, Credit Analyst, prepares the debt-to-income worksheet and collateral valuation. Our general guardrails are:
- Maximum debt-to-income ratio of 45 percent including the proposed payment.
- Maximum loan-to-value of 110 percent on new vehicles and 100 percent on used vehicles, using the valuation guide recorded in LoanDesk.
- Maximum term of 72 months for new vehicles and 60 months for used vehicles over 6 model years old.
- Minimum verified income documentation: two recent pay records or the most recent tax return for self-employed members.
- Vehicles over 12 model years old or with high mileage require manager approval.

Exceptions
An exception is any approval that departs from the guardrails above. The underwriter documents the compensating factors (for example, long membership tenure, strong share balance, or low existing debt) in LoanDesk. Exceptions up to 5 percentage points over the DTI limit can be approved by Rita. Anything larger, or any combination of two or more exceptions, comes to me. We track exception volume monthly and aim to keep it under 8 percent of funded auto loans.

Pricing
Rates are set by credit tier, term, and vehicle age using the rate sheet published by Lending at the start of each month. Relationship managers may apply the automatic payment discount and the direct deposit discount, but not both unless the sheet says so. Do not offer rate matches on your own. Send competitor offers to me with documentation.

Adverse Action and Fair Lending
If we deny or counter with less favorable terms, an adverse action notice must go out within the required timeframe. Compliance, led by Wesley Tran, reviews the template wording each quarter. Decisions must be based on the written criteria only. Never reference protected characteristics in notes, and do not steer members to particular products based on assumptions about them. Questions go to Compliance before the decision is communicated.

Funding and Booking
After approval, the relationship manager confirms lien instructions and the title process, then the loan is booked in CoreBanking through LoanDesk. Disbursement to a dealer or lienholder is processed by Operations. Rita Solano's team handles settlement, and Larry Bernard reconciles disbursements. Proceeds sent by ACH move through ACHHub, so check for any ACHHub incidents before promising a same-day funding time. Loans must not be funded until all conditions on the approval are cleared and the signed documents are in the file.

Post-Funding Review
The Lending team samples ten percent of funded auto loans each month for file completeness: authorization, income documents, valuation, signed disclosures, and lien perfection. Findings are logged and reviewed in the monthly Lending meeting. Missing lien paperwork older than 60 days is escalated to me.
